topic: Captain America Comics #1's 1940 Hitler-punch cover and the real Nazi death threats it caused
title: The 1940 Comic Cover That Got Its Own Creators Real Nazi Death Threats
description: AI-narrated commentary on the true story behind Captain America Comics #1's 1940 Hitler-punching cover, and the real death threats and police protection that followed. Sources below.

hook_candidates.text: In 1940, Captain America punched Hitler on a comic book cover. Then the phone calls started.
Captain America's Hitler punch wasn't a movie stunt. It got real people real death threats in 1940.
What happens when a comic book punches an actual dictator in the face?
Two comic artists once needed police protection over a single drawing of Captain America.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who's only ever seen Captain America in the Marvel movies, because they want to show them the real 1940s comic that got its actual creators death threats.
contradicted_belief: Most people think Captain America punched Hitler in a movie, not on a real 1940 comic book cover that caused actual death threats.
closing_comment: Wild that a real comic book cover got its own artists Nazi death threats a year before America even entered WWII. Makes you wonder what Simon and Kirby would think of the MCU today.

sources.note: Smithsonian confirms Captain America Comics #1 (Dec 1940) shows Cap punching Hitler, before the US entered WWII.
US Holocaust Memorial Museum confirms the anti-Nazi cover and creators Joe Simon and Jack Kirby, both Jewish Americans.
